title: Mobility pressure is jointly patterned by place, household resources, and trip purpose
source_unit: 2022 NHTS household, person, and travel-day trip records joined by HOUSEID and grouped by URBRUR and HHFAMINC bands

denominator.unit: weighted household percentage base; trip measures use weighted recorded trips

observations.method: Weighted descriptive cell using WTHHFIN for household measures and WTTRDFIN for travel-day trip measures. Work trips are WHYTRP90=01; shopping trips are TRIPPURP=04.
observations.uncertainty: No design-based interval is reproduced; the low-income urban cell contains 774 household records and 448 shopping-trip records. HHFAMINC bands are broad and household income is categorical.
observations.counterinterpretation: High zero-vehicle prevalence does not prove unmet work or care access; the travel-day trip file does not observe all trips, fares, cancellations, or household coping.

denominator.unit: weighted household percentage base; trip measures use weighted recorded trips

observations.method: Same weighted cell method as the companion low-income urban observation.
observations.uncertainty: No design-based interval is reproduced; the high-income urban cell contains 2,681 household records and 2,532 shopping-trip records. Income is not a measure of liquid cash or transport affordability.
observations.counterinterpretation: More vehicles and higher income can coexist with long work commutes and high time burdens; recorded trip time does not establish whether the burden is voluntary or constrained.

denominator.unit: weighted household percentage base; trip measures use weighted recorded trips

observations.method: Same weighted cell method as the companion urban observations.
observations.uncertainty: No design-based interval is reproduced; the low-income rural cell contains 235 household records and 126 shopping-trip records. Small cells and broad rural classification limit precision.
observations.counterinterpretation: Lower recorded work-trip time than other cells does not establish better access; selection into observed trips and unobserved missed or substituted trips remain unknown.

denominator.unit: weighted household percentage base; trip measures use weighted recorded trips

observations.method: Same weighted cell method as the companion urban observations.
observations.uncertainty: No design-based interval is reproduced; the high-income rural cell contains 721 household records and 807 shopping-trip records. Long-trip estimates may be sensitive to the travel-day sample and extreme values.
observations.counterinterpretation: Vehicle availability does not remove geographic distance or make long commutes cheap in time, fuel, maintenance, or risk.

boundary: This is a descriptive 2022 cross-sectional screen, not a causal estimate or a complete care-access measure. Household income, vehicle count, work status, and recorded trip time are distinct variables; they do not jointly identify affordability, necessity, unmet trips, or welfare. Work and shopping trips are used as daily-life proxies, while care, medical, childcare, and social obligations require a dedicated linked calendar layer. The raw NHTS archive is externally retrieved and hash-identified; derived slices are temporary and not committed.
